overview:
Ron Estes seeks another term in a south-central Kansas district that leans heavily Republican, about twelve points to the right of the nation. He enters the general election with a large financial advantage, roughly $1.8 million raised and $1.7 million on hand, while Democrat Katy Tyndell has raised about $234,000. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so expectations rest on the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and money. Prediction markets give Estes a strong edge, pricing Democratic chances near seven percent. The seat is expected to remain Republican, though the margin of victory may depend on turnout and any late outside spending.
